pages.digitalTwinUseCases.approachP1: VHT.ai's digital twin is powered by ECHNA, our ethical-by-design clinical AI. Every data source — Apple HealthKit, lab results, immunizations, conditions, medications, wearables, member-reported entries — flows through the same hardened, consent-governed pipeline. Members see one orbital view of their health pillars; clinicians see a complete longitudinal record; nothing leaves the system without explicit, revocable consent.
pages.digitalTwinUseCases.approachP2: The result is a digital health twin that is clinically grounded, privacy-preserving, and useful from day one — whether you're managing a chronic condition, recovering from surgery, optimizing performance, or simply trying to stay ahead of avoidable risk.

pages.digitalTwinUseCases.faqs[0].a: A digital health twin is a continuously updated virtual model of an individual's physiology, behavior, and care history. It synthesizes data from wearables, electronic health records, lab results, genetics, and self-reported inputs to simulate how that specific person is likely to respond to interventions — enabling personalized, proactive care.
pages.digitalTwinUseCases.faqs[0].q: What is a digital health twin?
pages.digitalTwinUseCases.faqs[1].a: A health app typically tracks isolated metrics (steps, sleep, weight) and shows you graphs. A digital twin models the relationships between those metrics and your medical context, predicts trajectories, and personalizes recommendations to your individual baseline rather than population averages.
pages.digitalTwinUseCases.faqs[1].q: How is a digital twin different from a regular health app?
pages.digitalTwinUseCases.faqs[2].a: VHT.ai's digital twin is HIPAA-aligned, encrypted in transit and at rest, and governed by explicit consent for every data source. You decide which providers, family members, or research programs see which slices of your twin — and you can revoke access at any time.
pages.digitalTwinUseCases.faqs[2].q: Is my data private and secure inside a digital twin?
pages.digitalTwinUseCases.faqs[3].a: People managing chronic conditions, post-operative recovery, complex medication regimens, mental-health journeys, or aging-in-place see the largest immediate benefit. Healthy users gain personalized prevention and early-warning detection that traditional annual checkups cannot match.
pages.digitalTwinUseCases.faqs[3].q: Who benefits most from a digital health twin today?
pages.digitalTwinUseCases.faqs[4].a: No. A digital twin augments your care team by giving them a continuous, contextual view of your health between visits. Clinical decisions remain with your licensed providers; the twin makes those decisions better-informed and timelier.
pages.digitalTwinUseCases.faqs[4].q: Does a digital twin replace my doctor?
pages.digitalTwinUseCases.headline: Digital Health Twin Use Cases: 10 Real-World Applications
pages.digitalTwinUseCases.keywords: digital health twin use cases, digital twin healthcare, virtual patient model, personalized medicine, predictive healthcare
pages.digitalTwinUseCases.lede: A digital health twin is a living, continuously updated virtual model of one person's physiology, behavior, and care history. Below are ten of the most impactful ways this technology is changing how individuals, clinicians, and health systems deliver care today.
pages.digitalTwinUseCases.seoDescription: Ten concrete ways digital health twins are transforming chronic disease, recovery, mental health, prevention, athletic performance, clinical trials, elder care, and population health.
pages.digitalTwinUseCases.useCases[0].bo: For people living with diabetes, hypertension, COPD, or heart failure, a digital health twin continuously models how diet, activity, sleep, medication adherence, and lab values interact. Clinicians and members can see early warning signals — a creeping HbA1c trend, a widening blood-pressure variability — weeks before a traditional checkup would catch them, and adjust care plans proactively instead of reactively.
pages.digitalTwinUseCases.useCases[1].bo: A twin tracks every prescription, refill cadence, and side-effect report alongside biometric response. It flags missed doses, predicts adherence drop-off, surfaces drug-drug and drug-food interactions in context, and helps prescribers titrate doses based on the individual's own response curve rather than population averages.
pages.digitalTwinUseCases.useCases[2].bo: By combining family history, genetic risk, lifestyle, and longitudinal vitals, a digital health twin generates a personalized prevention roadmap: which screenings matter most for this individual this year, which immunizations are due, and which modifiable risk factors will move the needle most on 10-year outcomes.
pages.digitalTwinUseCases.useCases[3].bo: After surgery or hospital discharge, the twin monitors wound healing inputs, pain trajectory, mobility (steps, gait), sleep quality, and vital signs. Deviations from the expected recovery curve trigger early outreach — preventing readmissions that account for billions in avoidable healthcare spend each year.
pages.digitalTwinUseCases.useCases[4].bo: Mood, sleep architecture, heart-rate variability, social activity, and self-reported symptoms feed a twin model that detects depressive and anxious episodes earlier than periodic clinic visits. It supports therapists with continuity-of-care context and gives members validated coping tools tuned to their patterns.
pages.digitalTwinUseCases.useCases[5].bo: Athletes and active members use digital twins to balance training load with recovery. The twin integrates HRV, resting heart rate, sleep, hydration, and workout intensity to recommend when to push, when to deload, and when an emerging overtraining pattern needs intervention before injury.
pages.digitalTwinUseCases.useCases[6].bo: Twins make it dramatically easier to match patients to trials they actually qualify for, and to simulate virtual control arms. This shortens trial timelines, reduces participant burden, and expands access to investigational therapies for under-represented populations.
pages.digitalTwinUseCases.useCases[7].bo: For older adults, the twin watches for the small, gradual shifts that precede falls, cognitive decline, frailty, or polypharmacy harm. Family members and care teams get a shared, privacy-respecting view of changes — supporting independence longer and intervening before a crisis.
pages.digitalTwinUseCases.useCases[8].bo: Pediatric twins track growth percentiles, developmental milestones, immunization schedules, and family-history risk in one model. Parents see what to watch for at each stage; pediatricians get a richer longitudinal picture than periodic well-child visits alone can provide.
pages.digitalTwinUseCases.useCases[9].bo: At the system level, aggregated, de-identified twin data lets health plans, employers, and public-health agencies identify rising risk in specific cohorts, target outreach, and measure intervention impact in near-real-time — without waiting for claims-data lag of 90+ days.
pages.digitalTwinUseCases.whatBody: Borrowed from aerospace and manufacturing, the digital-twin concept models a real-world entity in software so engineers can simulate, predict, and optimize its behavior. Applied to health, the "entity" is you: your vitals, labs, medications, conditions, genetic risk, lifestyle, sleep, activity, mental health, and family history. A digital health twin keeps that model current and uses it to answer questions a traditional medical record cannot: What is likely to happen next? What change would help most? What is unusual for this person specifically?

pages.featureAppleHealth.ctaTitle: Put your Apple Health data to work
pages.featureAppleHealth.disclaimerBody: VHT and ECHNA help you understand your health data. They do not diagnose or treat any condition. If you think you may have a medical emergency, call your local emergency number.
pages.featureAppleHealth.faqs[0].a: VHT reads the Apple Health categories you allow and shows them as charts with an ECHNA analysis under each one. You can also ask ECHNA questions about your data in chat or by voice.
pages.featureAppleHealth.faqs[0].q: Which app can read my Apple Health data and explain it?
pages.featureAppleHealth.faqs[1].a: Yes. Apple Watch writes to Apple Health, and VHT reads from Apple Health, so steps, heart rate, workouts, sleep and other watch data come through.
pages.featureAppleHealth.faqs[1].q: Does it work with Apple Watch?
pages.featureAppleHealth.faqs[2].a: When you open the app and the data is more than 30 minutes old, once a day, through background updates for some data types, and whenever you tap Refresh.
pages.featureAppleHealth.faqs[3].a: Yes. The first sync covers 180 days, which is what the free Basic plan includes. On a paid plan you can extend it in settings to one, two or five years, and pause or resume the import.
pages.featureAppleHealth.faqs[3].q: Can I import my older Apple Health history?
pages.featureAppleHealth.faqs[4].a: Yes. The Android app syncs from Health Connect and is in testing on Google Play.
pages.featureAppleHealth.faqs[5].a: Yes. You choose the categories in the Apple Health permission sheet, and you can add or remove them at any time in the Health app.
pages.featureAppleHealth.faqs[5].q: Can I control what VHT sees?
pages.featureAppleHealth.headline: Apple Health sync: your iPhone and Apple Watch data, explained
pages.featureAppleHealth.highlights[0]: You pick which Apple Health categories to share, and can change them later
pages.featureAppleHealth.highlights[1]: Syncs on its own when you open the app, plus a daily catch-up
pages.featureAppleHealth.highlights[2]: Brings in 180 days of history on the free Basic plan, up to five years on paid plans
pages.featureAppleHealth.keywords: Apple Health app, Apple Health sync, apps that work with Apple Health, Apple Watch health data app, HealthKit app, Apple Health AI, health data dashboard, Health Connect app
pages.featureAppleHealth.lede: Your iPhone and Apple Watch already count steps, sleep and heart rate. VHT brings that data into one health record and asks ECHNA, its AI health assistant, to explain what the trends mean for you, next to your conditions, medications and goals.
pages.featureAppleHealth.limits[0]: Apple Health only runs on iPhone, so the sync needs the VHT iPhone app. The web shows data from your last phone sync.
pages.featureAppleHealth.limits[1]: If you log a value by hand for a day, your entry wins over the synced one for that day.
pages.featureAppleHealth.limits[2]: A heart rate or rhythm notification from your watch is not a diagnosis. Talk to a clinician about it.
pages.featureAppleHealth.limits[3]: You can turn off any category in the Health app at any time.
pages.featureAppleHealth.screenAlt: VHT Activity screen showing a 14-day daily steps chart with an ECHNA analysis below it
pages.featureAppleHealth.sections[0].bod: Activity (steps, active energy, distance, flights climbed, exercise and stand time), workouts, heart rate, resting heart rate and heart rate variability, blood pressure, blood oxygen, blood glucose, weight and body composition, sleep stages, mindful minutes, respiratory readings and cycle tracking. On iOS 16.4 or later it can also read the medications you track in the Health app. Data from an Apple Watch or another device that writes to Apple Health comes along with it.
pages.featureAppleHealth.sections[0].tit: What VHT reads from Apple Health
pages.featureAppleHealth.sections[1].bod: Each metric gets a chart with your average, trend, best and lowest day over 7 days, 14 days, 30 days, months or all time. Below the chart, ECHNA writes a short analysis that reads the numbers against your own profile: your age, conditions and goals, not a generic average.
pages.featureAppleHealth.sections[2].bod: Synced data counts toward the Lifestyle and Biometrics pillars of your Health Index and toward goals such as a daily step or sleep target, so progress updates without typing anything in.
pages.featureAppleHealth.sections[2].tit: It feeds your Health Index and goals
pages.featureAppleHealth.sections[3].bod: Ask “Why has my resting heart rate gone up?” or “How did I sleep this month?” and ECHNA answers from your recent synced history, by text or by voice. She explains and suggests next steps; she does not diagnose.
pages.featureAppleHealth.sections[4].bod: The Android app syncs from Health Connect into the same record. It is in testing on Google Play right now. On the web, you see the Apple Health and Android data from your last phone sync.

pages.featureCalorieTracker.ctaTitle: Track what you eat, and what it means
pages.featureCalorieTracker.disclaimerBo: VHT and ECHNA give general information to help you understand your habits. They do not diagnose or treat any condition, and they do not replace advice from a clinician or registered dietitian.
pages.featureCalorieTracker.faqs[0].a: Meal logging is part of every VHT plan, including the free Basic plan. The beta members we invite have Premium during the beta.
pages.featureCalorieTracker.faqs[0].q: Is VHT a free calorie counter?
pages.featureCalorieTracker.faqs[1].a: Yes. Each meal can record protein, carbs, fat, sugar and fiber, and optionally mono- and polyunsaturated fat and a set of vitamins and minerals.
pages.featureCalorieTracker.faqs[1].q: Does it track macros as well as calories?
pages.featureCalorieTracker.faqs[2].a: Not today. You log meals by picking a common food, using a favorite, or typing your own values.
pages.featureCalorieTracker.faqs[2].q: Can I take a photo of my food?
pages.featureCalorieTracker.faqs[3].a: Yes. Active energy from Apple Health and the calories from workouts you log show up in your activity data, next to what you ate.
pages.featureCalorieTracker.faqs[4].a: ECHNA can explain your eating pattern and suggest practical changes that fit your goals and health record. She does not prescribe a medical diet. For that, talk to your clinician or a registered dietitian.
pages.featureCalorieTracker.faqs[4].q: Can the AI tell me what to eat?
pages.featureCalorieTracker.headline: A calorie and macro tracker that knows the rest of your health
pages.featureCalorieTracker.highlights[0: Calories plus protein, carbs, fat, sugar and fiber for every meal
pages.featureCalorieTracker.highlights[1: Quick picks, favorites and one-tap meal combos for the foods you eat often
pages.featureCalorieTracker.highlights[2: ECHNA reads your food log alongside your activity and health record
pages.featureCalorieTracker.keywords: calorie tracker, calorie counter app, macro tracker, food diary app, meal tracker, protein tracker, nutrition tracker with AI, calories in calories out
pages.featureCalorieTracker.lede: Most calorie counters only see your food. In VHT, your meals sit next to your activity, sleep, weight, lab results and conditions, so ECHNA can tell you what your eating pattern means for you, not for an average person.
pages.featureCalorieTracker.limits[0]: Meals are entered by you. VHT does not scan barcodes or recognize food from photos today.
pages.featureCalorieTracker.limits[1]: Calorie and macro numbers are only as accurate as what you enter.
pages.featureCalorieTracker.limits[2]: ECHNA gives general nutrition guidance. For a medical diet, such as for kidney disease or an eating disorder, work with a clinician or registered dietitian.

Choose breakfast, lunch, dinner or a snack, then pick a common food from the quick-pick list or type your own meal with its calories and macros. Optional fields cover mono- and polyunsaturated fat and micronutrients such as vitamin C, zinc and selenium when you want more detail.
Log a meal in a few taps
Save any meal as a favorite and log it again with one tap. If you eat the same breakfast most days, log your whole favorite breakfast as a single combo.
Favorites and combos for the meals you repeat
Calories burned come in from Apple Health and your logged workouts, so your intake and your activity sit side by side. Drinks have their own log for water, caffeine, sugar and alcohol.
Food and activity in the same place
Every log has a calendar view with a monthly chart and average, and you can tap any day to see what you logged. ECHNA can look back over your recent meals when you ask about them.
Ask ECHNA “Am I eating enough protein?” or “How do my meals affect my blood sugar?” She answers from your own food log, goals and conditions, such as type 2 diabetes or high cholesterol, and suggests small, practical changes.
Advice that fits your health record

pages.featureSymptomTracker.ctaBody: Join the beta to start a symptom diary that sits next to your conditions, medications and daily data, with ECHNA to help you make sense of it.
pages.featureSymptomTracker.ctaTitle: Bring the whole story to your next appointment
pages.featureSymptomTracker.disclaimerBo: VHT and ECHNA do not diagnose or treat any condition. If you think you may have a medical emergency, call your local emergency number or go to the nearest emergency department.
pages.featureSymptomTracker.faqs[0].a: Log each symptom when it happens, with the date, how severe it was and anything that might have triggered it. A dated record is far more useful to a clinician than a description from memory. VHT keeps that record and ECHNA can summarize it before your visit.
pages.featureSymptomTracker.faqs[0].q: What is the best way to track symptoms for my doctor?
pages.featureSymptomTracker.faqs[1].a: No. VHT and ECHNA help you record and understand your symptoms, and ECHNA can explain possible general reasons and when to seek care. Only a clinician can diagnose the cause.
pages.featureSymptomTracker.faqs[1].q: Can VHT tell me what is causing my symptoms?
pages.featureSymptomTracker.faqs[2].a: Yes. Link symptoms to a condition in your record, such as migraine, asthma or irritable bowel syndrome, and note the triggers. Over time you can see how often flares happen and what tends to come before them.
pages.featureSymptomTracker.faqs[2].q: Can I track symptoms for a chronic condition?
pages.featureSymptomTracker.faqs[3].a: Yes. Symptoms you log in the Apple Health app sync into VHT on iPhone, alongside the ones you log in VHT.
pages.featureSymptomTracker.faqs[3].q: Does it sync symptoms from Apple Health?
pages.featureSymptomTracker.faqs[4].a: Symptom logging is part of Quick Log, which is included in every VHT plan, including the free Basic plan.

pages.featureSymptomTracker.highlights[1: Severity, body location and notes on every entry
pages.featureSymptomTracker.highlights[2: Link a symptom to a condition you already track, with its triggers
pages.featureSymptomTracker.keywords: symptom tracker, symptom tracker app, symptom diary, symptom journal, track symptoms for doctor, chronic illness tracker, migraine tracker, flare tracker
pages.featureSymptomTracker.lede: “When did this start, and how often does it happen?” is hard to answer from memory. VHT keeps a dated record of your symptoms next to your conditions, medications, sleep and activity, so you and your clinician can see the pattern.
pages.featureSymptomTracker.limits[0]: A symptom tracker records what you feel. It does not tell you what is causing it.
pages.featureSymptomTracker.limits[1]: Chest pain, trouble breathing, fainting, or sudden weakness or confusion can be an emergency. Call your local emergency number instead of logging it.
pages.featureSymptomTracker.limits[2]: If a symptom is new, getting worse or worrying you, contact a clinician. Do not wait for a pattern.
pages.featureSymptomTracker.screenAlt: VHT Medical card showing a Medical score of 58 with counts of conditions, allergies, medications and supplements
Tap Symptom in the Quick Log bar, pick what you feel, from headache, fatigue and dizziness to heartburn, coughing or a racing heartbeat, and rate it as none, mild, moderate or severe. Add where it hurts and a short note if you like. You can also log it for an earlier day.
If the symptom belongs to a condition you already have, such as migraine or asthma, link it and note what triggered it. If it is new and you do not know the cause, you can start tracking it as a new concern to raise with your clinician. VHT does not diagnose it.
Every symptom appears on your calendar with a monthly chart, so you can see how often it happens and whether it lines up with poor sleep, a new medication or a stressful week.
See the pattern on a calendar
If you already log symptoms in the Apple Health app, VHT syncs them into the same record, so nothing is entered twice.
Symptoms from Apple Health come in too
ECHNA can see your last 90 days of symptoms. Ask “What should I tell my doctor about my headaches?” and she can summarize when they happened, how severe they were and what else was going on, so you walk into the appointment with facts instead of guesses.
pages.featureSymptomTracker.seoDescripti: Log symptoms with severity, body location and notes, link them to a condition, and see them on a calendar. ECHNA, an AI health assistant, helps you spot patterns and prepare for your clinician.

pages.labPanels.panels.cbc.faqs[0].a: No. Food does not affect a CBC. If ferritin, iron or other tests are drawn at the same time, your clinician may ask you to fast or come in the morning.
pages.labPanels.panels.cbc.faqs[0].q: Do I need to fast for a CBC?
pages.labPanels.panels.cbc.faqs[1].a: Yes. Iron stores run down before hemoglobin falls, so ferritin can be low while the CBC still looks normal. Tiredness, hair shedding or restless legs can appear at this stage.
pages.labPanels.panels.cbc.faqs[1].q: Can I have iron deficiency with a normal hemoglobin?
pages.labPanels.panels.cbc.faqs[2].a: MCV is the average size of your red cells; MCH is the average amount of hemoglobin in each one. They usually move together: both are low in iron deficiency and both are high when B12 or folate is low.
pages.labPanels.panels.cbc.faqs[2].q: What is the difference between MCV and MCH?
pages.labPanels.panels.cbc.faqs[3].a: Not before the cause is known. Iron taken when you do not need it can build up in the body, and starting iron or B12 can blur later tests. Talk to your clinician about which test comes next.

pages.labPanels.panels.cbc.lede: A complete blood count (CBC) is one of the most common blood tests. It counts your red cells, white cells and platelets and describes the size and color of your red cells. When something looks off, ferritin and vitamin B12 are often the next tests. This page explains how they connect. Each marker has its own detailed guide.
pages.labPanels.panels.cbc.sections[0].b: A CBC reports hemoglobin and the red cell count, the white cell count (often with a breakdown of the different types) and platelets. It also lists red cell indices: MCV (average size), MCH and MCHC (hemoglobin per cell) and RDW (variation in size). These indices help explain why hemoglobin is low or high.
pages.labPanels.panels.cbc.sections[1].b: Clinicians often sort anemia by red cell size. Small, pale cells (low MCV and MCH) most often point to iron deficiency, which ferritin can confirm. Large cells (high MCV and MCH) can come from low vitamin B12 or folate, heavy alcohol use, liver disease, an underactive thyroid or some medicines. A high RDW adds that the cells are a mix of sizes, which can show up early, before hemoglobin falls.
pages.labPanels.panels.cbc.sections[2].b: Ferritin shows how much iron your body has stored, and a low ferritin confirms iron deficiency even when hemoglobin is still normal. Vitamin B12 is checked when red cells are large or there are symptoms such as tingling, numbness or memory problems. Finding the cause matters: in adults, iron deficiency often leads to a search for blood loss.
pages.labPanels.panels.cbc.sections[2].t: Why ferritin and B12 are checked next
pages.labPanels.panels.cbc.sections[3].b: Recent infection, pregnancy, heavy periods, endurance training, smoking, living at high altitude and dehydration can all shift CBC values. Inflammation can raise ferritin and hide low iron stores, so ferritin is often read together with CRP.
pages.labPanels.panels.cbc.sections[3].t: What else can change a CBC
pages.labPanels.panels.cbc.sections[4].b: A CBC also checks white cells, which fight infection, and platelets, which help blood clot. Values just outside the range are common and often settle on a repeat test. Values far outside the range, or several abnormal values together, need prompt follow-up with your clinician.

pages.labPanels.panels.diabetes.cardDesc: HbA1c and fasting glucose: how the two tests screen for prediabetes and diabetes, and why results are confirmed.
pages.labPanels.panels.diabetes.ctaBody: Add your results to VHT to see HbA1c and glucose side by side across the years, and ECHNA, your AI health assistant, explains what changed in plain language.
pages.labPanels.panels.diabetes.ctaTitle: Follow your blood sugar over time
No. HbA1c reflects the past two to three months, so a recent meal does not change it. Fasting glucose does need at least eight hours without food or drinks other than water.
Do I need to fast for an HbA1c test?
Often, yes. Losing a modest amount of weight if you carry extra, being active most days and eating fewer refined carbohydrates bring blood sugar back into the normal range for many people. Rechecking at least once a year shows whether it is working.
Many guidelines suggest screening adults from age 35, or earlier with risk factors such as excess weight, a family history of diabetes or diabetes in a past pregnancy, and repeating every three years if results are normal. People living with diabetes usually have HbA1c checked every three to six months.
How often should blood sugar be checked?
A fasting glucose below 100 mg/dL (5.6 mmol/L) is usually normal. Levels below 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L) are low and, with symptoms such as shakiness, sweating or confusion, need prompt attention.
What is a normal fasting blood sugar?

pages.labPanels.panels.diabetes.lede: Two blood tests do most of the work in checking for prediabetes and diabetes: HbA1c, which reflects your average blood sugar over about three months, and fasting glucose, a snapshot of one morning. This page explains how they fit together. Each test has its own detailed guide.
pages.labPanels.panels.diabetes.sections: HbA1c and fasting glucose look at blood sugar in different ways, so they do not always agree. HbA1c smooths out day-to-day swings, while fasting glucose shows how well your body keeps sugar in check overnight. Either can be used for screening, and together they give a fuller picture.

Diabetes is usually diagnosed at an HbA1c of 6.5% (48 mmol/mol) or higher, or a fasting glucose of 126 mg/dL (7.0 mmol/L) or higher. The prediabetes range is an HbA1c of 5.7 to 6.4% (39 to 47 mmol/mol) or a fasting glucose of 100 to 125 mg/dL (5.6 to 6.9 mmol/L). Some countries use slightly different prediabetes cut-offs.

Unless you have clear symptoms of high blood sugar, a single abnormal result is normally repeated before a diagnosis is made, either with the same test on another day or with the other test. Illness, stress and some medicines can push glucose up for a while.

Anything that changes red blood cells, such as anemia, recent blood loss or transfusion, some hemoglobin variants, kidney disease or pregnancy, can make HbA1c read higher or lower than your true average. In those cases clinicians lean more on glucose tests, including an oral glucose tolerance test.

An oral glucose tolerance test measures blood sugar two hours after a sweet drink. People living with diabetes also tend to have kidney checks (eGFR and urine albumin), a lipid panel and regular eye and foot exams, because diabetes affects blood vessels throughout the body.

pages.labPanels.panels.kidneyLiverInflam: eGFR, ALT, CRP and ESR: what they show about your kidneys, liver and inflammation, and why they are read together.
Add your results to VHT to follow eGFR, ALT, CRP and ESR side by side, and ECHNA, your AI health assistant, explains what changed in plain language.
Watch your kidneys, liver and inflammation over time

eGFR, ALT, CRP and ESR do not usually need fasting. If glucose or a lipid panel is drawn at the same time, you may be asked to fast. Avoid a very hard workout the day before, since it can raise ALT and CRP for a while.
Do I need to fast for these tests?

An eGFR of 90 or above is normal, and 60 to 89 can be normal for older adults when there are no other signs of kidney damage. A result below 60 for three months or more meets the definition of chronic kidney disease.
What is a normal eGFR?

Usually it is mild and has a common cause such as fatty liver, alcohol or a medicine. Very high values, or a raised ALT with yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine or belly pain, need prompt medical attention.
Is a high ALT serious?
Your clinician chooses. CRP is better for following a fast-changing problem such as an infection; ESR is often used for some long-term inflammatory conditions. Many clinicians order both.
Should I get CRP or ESR?
Kidney, Liver and Inflammation Tests Explained: eGFR, ALT, CRP and ESR
kidney function test, liver function test, inflammation blood test, eGFR ALT CRP ESR, comprehensive metabolic panel explained, CMP blood test, kidney and liver blood tests

eGFR and ALT come from the chemistry part of a routine blood panel and show how your kidneys and liver are doing. CRP and ESR are separate tests that look for inflammation anywhere in the body. This page explains how they fit together. Each test has its own detailed guide.

eGFR and ALT usually appear on a comprehensive metabolic panel (CMP), along with sodium, potassium, glucose, creatinine and other liver tests such as AST, ALP and bilirubin. CRP and ESR are ordered on their own, often when symptoms suggest an infection or an inflammatory condition, or to follow one over time.
Where these tests come from

eGFR shows filtering capacity, but kidney damage can show up first as protein in the urine. That is why people with diabetes or high blood pressure are usually checked with both eGFR and a urine albumin test. A low eGFR is confirmed on a repeat test, because dehydration, a large meat meal or intense exercise can lower it for a while.
Kidneys: eGFR with a urine test

A mildly raised ALT is common and often linked to fatty liver, alcohol, some medicines and supplements, or a recent hard workout. Clinicians read it with AST, ALP and bilirubin to see which part of the liver is involved, and usually recheck it before looking further.
Liver: ALT in context

CRP and ESR both rise with inflammation but on different time scales. CRP moves within hours and falls quickly with recovery; ESR changes over days to weeks. Neither says where the inflammation is, so they are read with symptoms, an examination and other results, including the CBC.
Inflammation: CRP and ESR together

Organs affect each other's numbers. Inflammation can raise ferritin; a serious illness or dehydration can lower eGFR for a while; fatty liver often comes with high triglycerides and blood sugar; and long-term kidney disease can cause anemia. Looking at the whole picture over time, rather than one value, gives the most reliable view.
Why these results connect

pages.labPanels.panels.lipid.ctaBody: Add your results to VHT to follow LDL, HDL and triglycerides over time, and ECHNA, your AI health assistant, explains what changed in plain language.
pages.labPanels.panels.lipid.ctaTitle: See your whole lipid panel in one place
pages.labPanels.panels.lipid.faqs[0].a: Many labs flag these as desirable for adults: total cholesterol below 200 mg/dL (5.2 mmol/L), LDL below 100 mg/dL (2.6 mmol/L), HDL of 40 mg/dL (1.0 mmol/L) or more in men and 50 mg/dL (1.3 mmol/L) or more in women, and triglycerides below 150 mg/dL (1.7 mmol/L). Your own LDL target depends on your overall risk, so it may be lower.
pages.labPanels.panels.lipid.faqs[0].q: What is a normal cholesterol level?
pages.labPanels.panels.lipid.faqs[1].a: It is total cholesterol minus HDL. It captures LDL plus other particles that can build up in arteries, and it stays reliable when you have not fasted or your triglycerides are high. Many clinicians use it alongside LDL.
pages.labPanels.panels.lipid.faqs[2].a: Often by some amount. Eating less saturated fat and more fiber, vegetables and whole grains, staying active, keeping a healthy weight and limiting alcohol can improve LDL and triglycerides. Whether that is enough depends on your numbers and overall risk, which is a decision to make with your clinician.
pages.labPanels.panels.lipid.faqs[2].q: Can I lower my cholesterol without medicine?
pages.labPanels.panels.lipid.faqs[3].a: Labs outside the United States usually report lipids in mmol/L. To convert cholesterol from mg/dL, divide by 38.67; for triglycerides, divide by 88.57. Always compare against the reference range printed on your own report.
pages.labPanels.panels.lipid.faqs[3].q: Why does my report show mmol/L?

pages.labPanels.panels.lipid.lede: A lipid panel, often just called a cholesterol test, measures the fats in your blood that matter most for heart and blood vessel health. This page explains what is on the report, how to prepare and how clinicians read the numbers together. Each marker has its own detailed guide.
pages.labPanels.panels.lipid.sections[0]: A standard panel reports total cholesterol, LDL cholesterol, HDL cholesterol and triglycerides. Many reports also show non-HDL cholesterol (total cholesterol minus HDL), which counts all the cholesterol carried in particles that can build up in arteries. LDL is often calculated from the other values rather than measured directly.
What is on a lipid panel?
pages.labPanels.panels.lipid.sections[1]: For most people a non-fasting test is fine for a routine check, and many guidelines now accept it. Triglycerides rise after a meal, so if they come back high, or your clinician needs a precise LDL, you may be asked to repeat the test after fasting for 8 to 12 hours. Water is fine.
pages.labPanels.panels.lipid.sections[2]: No single value tells the whole story. A high LDL matters more when HDL is low, triglycerides are high or other risk factors are present, such as smoking, high blood pressure, diabetes, older age or a family history of early heart disease. Clinicians often enter the panel into a risk calculator that estimates the chance of a heart attack or stroke over the next ten years.
How the numbers are read together
pages.labPanels.panels.lipid.sections[3]: Recent illness, pregnancy, some medicines (including steroids, some diuretics and hormone treatments), an underactive thyroid, poorly controlled diabetes, kidney disease and heavy drinking can all shift the numbers. A very high LDL from a young age can point to familial hypercholesterolemia, an inherited condition that is worth knowing about because it runs in families.
pages.labPanels.panels.lipid.sections[4]: Healthy adults are often checked every four to six years, and more often if results are borderline, other risk factors are present or treatment starts or changes. After starting a cholesterol-lowering medicine, a repeat test after one to three months shows how well it is working.

pages.labResultsHub.howTo[0].body: Ranges differ between labs, methods and units (for example mg/dL or mmol/L). The range printed next to your result is the one that applies to it.
pages.labResultsHub.howTo[0].title: Use your lab's reference range
pages.labResultsHub.howTo[1].body: Reference ranges are usually set so that about 1 in 20 healthy people falls outside them on any single test. A result slightly out of range is common; a steady change over several tests says more.
pages.labResultsHub.howTo[1].title: Look at the trend, not one number

pages.research.projects.treatmentPlan.bu: A layered RAG pipeline: vector stores over roughly 512,000 de-identified patient-like records and about 425,000 PubMed documents, similarity retrieval at each layer, and a language model that drafts a plan from the retrieved evidence.
pages.research.projects.treatmentPlan.im: Student team and VHT staff beside the treatment-plan AI poster at the Northeastern University Vancouver showcase, spring 2025.
pages.research.projects.treatmentPlan.in: Northeastern University Vancouver, Khoury College of Computer Sciences
pages.research.projects.treatmentPlan.qu: Can a retrieval-augmented stack find similar patient cases and PubMed literature, then draft a structured, evidence-aware treatment plan with measurable retrieval quality at every layer?
pages.research.projects.treatmentPlan.re: Plan quality averaged BERTScore F1 0.796 (best 0.873) against reference plans; patient-case retrieval reached Precision@10 of 1.0 on all ten test cases.
Evaluation on research data by the student team; not a measure of the VHT product.
pages.research.projects.tribunal.built: A three-judge scoring layer built on open-weight medical and general models, a 50-example expert-annotated set, and a rule corpus of 20 rules and 143 documents drawn from WHO, UNESCO and NIST AI RMF guidance that drives the revision step.
pages.research.projects.tribunal.imageAl: Student team, faculty and VHT staff with the LLM Tribunal poster at the Northeastern University Vancouver showcase, spring 2026.
pages.research.projects.tribunal.institu: Northeastern University Vancouver, College of Engineering (MS in Data Analytics Engineering)
pages.research.projects.tribunal.questio: Can a panel of judge models score a medical AI answer on ethics, privacy, autonomy and accuracy, then guide a retrieval-based revision before it reaches a member?
pages.research.projects.tribunal.result: On the showcase question, ECHNA’s answer rose from 32/40 to 34/40 after Tribunal revision, with the privacy score moving from 6 to 8.
pages.research.projects.tribunal.resultN: Scores on the team’s own rubric, measured on research prompts; the student code is not part of the live ECHNA service.
pages.research.projects.tribunal.title: LLM Tribunal: scoring and revising ECHNA answers
pages.research.projects.uploadDefence.bu: A hybrid detector: a LightGBM classifier over structural PDF features for malware, and a locally hosted 8B language model that screens document text for injected instructions, packaged to run inside the platform boundary.
pages.research.projects.uploadDefence.im: Student team, faculty and VHT staff with the PDF malware and prompt-injection poster at Khoury College, Northeastern University Vancouver, spring 2026.
pages.research.projects.uploadDefence.in: Northeastern University Vancouver, Khoury College of Computer Sciences (CS 7980)
pages.research.projects.uploadDefence.qu: Can a local, HIPAA-compatible pipeline catch both classic PDF malware and prompt-injection text hidden in uploaded medical documents, without sending anything to cloud scanners?
pages.research.projects.uploadDefence.re: LightGBM reached 99.13% accuracy and 99.96% AUC-ROC (0.74% false-positive rate) on the public CIC-Evasive-PDFMal2022 set; the local model flagged 91% of injected documents at 1.36 s mean latency.
Public datasets and synthetic injections only, static analysis only; about 28% of benign documents were flagged for review by design. Not a product guarantee.
pages.research.projects.uvicDeterioratio: A multi-task transformer trained on the MIMIC-IV research database (about 100,000 admissions), with shared representations across six deterioration tasks and built-in explanations, co-supervised with our founder & CTO, Dean Shev, as industry advisor.
The graduate researcher and Dean Shev, VHT's founder & CTO, at a VHT demo table showing ECHNA on screen, 2025.
University of Victoria, Faculty of Engineering and Computer Science (MEng in Biomedical Systems)
Can one explainable multi-task transformer predict renal, cardiac, metabolic and perfusion deterioration jointly from hospital event sequences, fast enough for real-time use?
AUROC between 0.792 and 0.876 across the six tasks, with under 50 ms inference and 87% fewer parameters than eight single-task models.
Credentialed research data (MIMIC-IV), not VHT member data; nothing from this project runs in the VHT product.

VHT (Virtual Healthcare Technologies) is an AI-powered personal health platform that unifies your health data into a single secure record, then applies intelligent analysis to surface meaningful insights.

At the core is ECHNA — our Empathetic Care & Health Navigation Assistant — a conversational AI you can ask anything about your health: "What do my lab results mean?", "How is my sleep affecting my heart rate?", or "Am I hitting my weekly activity goals?"

The platform includes:
• Your Health Index — a six-pillar score (Lifestyle, Biometrics, Medical Profile, Genetics, Preventive, Environment) that gives you a single view of your overall health trajectory
• Digital Twin — a personalized health model built from your real data, updated continuously
• Apple HealthKit sync — automatic import of 150+ data types from your iPhone and Apple Watch
• Quick Log — 13 fast-entry modals for vitals, meals, sleep, symptoms, workouts, and more
• Medical Profile — conditions, medications, supplements, allergies, lab results, and immunizations in one place
pages.support.faqs[0].question: What is VHT and how does it work?
pages.support.faqs[10].answer:
The Health Index is a composite score from 0–100 that reflects your overall health across six pillars:

1. Lifestyle — activity, sleep, nutrition, stress, habits
2. Biometrics — vitals such as heart rate, blood pressure, BMI, HRV, and body composition
3. Medical Profile — conditions, medications, allergies, and lab results
4. Genetics — hereditary risk factors and family history
5. Preventive — immunizations, screenings, and preventive procedures
6. Environment — occupational exposures, living environment, and locality signals

Each pillar is scored individually based on your logged and synced data, then blended into your overall Health Index. The score updates as your data changes and is visible on your My Hub carousel. You can ask ECHNA "Explain my Health Index" for a detailed breakdown of what is driving your score.

Your Digital Twin is a continuously updated virtual model of your health, built entirely from your real data — vitals, lab results, HealthKit readings, medications, conditions, and more.

It serves as the data foundation that makes ECHNA's responses personalized and contextually accurate. When you ask ECHNA a question, she draws on your Digital Twin to give answers grounded in your actual health history, not generic population averages.

The Digital Twin matures over time as you add more data. A "data maturity" indicator in My Hub shows how complete your profile is across seven health domains: personal information and the six Health Index pillars.

Important: Most Bluetooth health devices sold on Amazon, AliExpress, and Temu — smart rings, fitness watches, blood pressure cuffs, smart scales, pulse oximeters, thermometers, and chest straps — are manufactured by Shenzhen-based ODMs (original design manufacturers) and resold under dozens of different brand names. BOZLUN, MAYNOS, AIWASI, Donerton, SLOTHCLOUD, ENGERWALL, FITINDEX, LAZLE, MMIZOO, EMAY, Zacurate, CONTEC, iProven, and many others. These devices almost always come with a companion app that the manufacturer tells you to install.

We strongly recommend that you DO NOT use these third-party companion apps for your health data. Here is why:

━━━ SECURITY RISKS — ACROSS ALL DEVICE TYPES ━━━

• No HIPAA compliance — White-label companion apps are not designed for health data privacy regulations. Whether it's a ring app storing your sleep data, a BP cuff app storing your blood pressure history, or a scale app storing your weight and body composition, these apps may keep your health data on unencrypted servers in jurisdictions with weak or non-existent data protection laws.

• No security audit — These apps are built by small firmware teams that prioritize cost over security. They rarely undergo independent security testing or code audits. The same factory that makes the hardware ships a companion app as an afterthought — the app exists so the product page can say "Includes free app."

• Data sharing unknown — Many white-label apps request broad permissions (contacts, location, photos, microphone) that have nothing to do with your BP readings or step count. Their privacy policies — if they exist at all — are often vague, machine-translated, or link to dead pages.

• Server locations unclear — Your health data may be stored on servers in countries with no equivalent to HIPAA or GDPR. You may have no legal right to request deletion, no way to verify your data was actually deleted, and no recourse if it is breached.

• Account creation required — Many white-label apps force you to create an account with an email or phone number just to use the device. This ties your health data to a permanent identity on servers you do not control.

━━━ SPECIFIC DEVICE CATEGORY RISKS ━━━

• Ring apps — often request location and contacts. Store sleep, HR, and activity data indefinitely.
• BP cuff apps — your blood pressure history is a direct medical record. Many apps store it unencrypted.
• Scale apps — body composition data (weight, BMI, body fat %) is personal health information that should be protected.
• Oximeter / thermometer apps — these collect real-time physiological readings with no privacy framework.
• Watch / band apps — often the worst offenders, requesting full phone permissions and syncing continuously.

━━━ VHT'S APPROACH ━━━

VHT connects directly to your device via Bluetooth — no companion app is ever involved. Your health data travels straight from the device to VHT's HIPAA-aligned infrastructure:

• Encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at rest (AES-256)
• Row-level security ensures only you can access your data
• No data ever sold to third parties or used for advertising
• You can request full account and data deletion at any time — and we verify it
• Built on Supabase, which holds a SOC 2 Type II report, with HIPAA-aligned security controls
• No account on any manufacturer's server — your data lives only where you choose

━━━ PRACTICAL ADVICE ━━━

If your device requires its companion app for initial setup (firmware updates, time sync, or calibration):

1. Install the app on an older phone or tablet that does not contain your personal health information, or
2. Install it temporarily for setup only, then immediately uninstall it before pairing with VHT, or
3. Skip the companion app entirely — most devices work with VHT out of the box without any app setup

Your health data deserves a health-grade platform — not a generic Bluetooth utility app from an unverified manufacturer.

All Bluetooth devices sync the same way through the VHT iOS app:

• Open Settings → Health Sync → Devices and tap "Scan for Devices"
• When your device appears, tap "Pair" (rings) or "Connect" (BP monitors, scales, etc.)
• VHT auto-detects your device and selects the correct connection method

pages.support.faqs[7].question: How does Apple HealthKit integration work?
pages.support.faqs[8].answer:
VHT is strictly read-only with respect to Apple Health.

When your iPhone prompts you to grant HealthKit permissions, VHT only requests read access. Write (share) permission is never requested and is explicitly set to nil in our iOS code — iOS will never allow VHT to create or modify any record in your Apple Health database.

Your Apple Health data is the authoritative source. VHT reads it, enriches it with clinical context and AI insights, and stores a secure copy in your VHT health record. Nothing ever flows back from VHT into Apple Health.
pages.support.faqs[8].question: Does VHT write anything back to Apple Health?
pages.support.faqs[9].answer:
On the iOS app, tap "Sign in with Apple" on the sign-in screen. This triggers the native iOS Face ID / Touch ID authentication sheet — no password required and your Apple ID email can be hidden.

Your Apple ID token is exchanged directly with VHT's secure backend. We never see your Apple ID password. If you hide your Apple email, Apple provides a private relay address that VHT uses to send any account-related emails.

Apple Sign-In is also available on the web via standard OAuth redirect.
